stances_toward.note: NATO co-member and, since the first intergovernmental summit in Rome (13 Nov 2025), a strategic partner: over a dozen accords on energy, defence industry, health, diaspora and migration; Meloni counts 3,000 Italian firms in Albania; Italy is the first trade partner (about 42% of exports, 2025) and the biggest tourist source after Kosovo (1.2 million visitors). Italy publicly backs Albania's EU entry ahead of Ukraine and Moldova (Feb 2026). The migration protocol (2023, converted into a repatriation centre in 2025) is the contested element: Advocate General Emiliou found it compatible with EU law (Apr 2026), Advocate General Medina set strict guarantees for detention outside the EU (Jun 2026), MEPs said they were blocked from a full inspection of Gjader (29 Jun 2026). Bond - affinity: trade, tourism and migration ties, not kinship.

sources.title: Italy-Albania intergovernmental summit: a historic day for bilateral relations
Balkans: Italy underlines support for Albania, Montenegro's swift EU entry
Advocate General says Italy-Albania migrant protocol is lawful in principle
EU lawmakers say they were blocked from fully inspecting Italy's migrant detention centre in Albania

stances_toward.note: Close and quarrelsome. Stocker met Meloni in Rome in July 2025 on migration (agreed: deportations, safe third countries), the South Tyrol autonomy statute revision (he thanked her) and the Brenner, where Italy 'categorically' refuses the cross-border truck slot system Vienna wants; Italy sued Austria at the EU Court in 2024 over the Tyrol truck bans (C-524/24) and the Advocate General found three of four measures unlawful on 16 Jul 2026. Italy is among Austria's biggest trading partners and its energy gateway (the gas that replaced Russia's). The old South Tyrol citizenship quarrel (2018) is dormant. Partner, not ally: Austria is neutral. Bond kin: South Tyrol, shared Habsburg history.

relations_to.summary: Protocol (Nov 2023) for Italian-run migrant centres at Shengjin and Gjader, converted in March 2025 into repatriation centres (about 620 detainees by mid-June 2026). Advocate General Emiliou (23 Apr 2026) found it compatible with EU law with safeguards; Advocate General Medina (June 2026) stressed that EU guarantees apply to detention outside the EU; the CJEU has not ruled.
